Indikator 10 is a national quality indicator in Denmark that measures the mortality rate among prevalent patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] during a specific reporting period [^src1]. It serves as a primary quantitative metric in the annual report from the Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark, providing detailed breakdowns of mortality data at the national, regional, and municipal levels [^src1]. 

The reporting period for Indikator 10 spans from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023 [^src1]. To calculate this metric, mortality is assessed for all prevalent patients who were alive as of July 1, 2022, and who had received an atrial fibrillation diagnosis registered in the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] at least once within the preceding 10 years [^src1]. The vital status of these patients (whether they are dead or alive) is determined through data linkage with the [[cpr-registeret|CPR-registeret]] [^src1]. 

Alongside Indikator 16, which tracks the incidence of heart failure among newly diagnosed patients, Indikator 10 forms a core component of the clinical quality development efforts overseen by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1]. The broad geographic coverage and methodological transparency of these indicators underscore their importance in evaluating and guiding the Danish healthcare system's management of atrial fibrillation [^src1].
